meetingLanguage (optional): The language for the meeting. Default is en-US.

title (required): The title of the meeting.
tags (optional): You can pass comma seprated va

data.name: Create a Meeting
data.description:
Creates/schedules a meeting. Use this endpoint to create scheduled meetings (or ad-hoc meetings when supported). The request body describes meeting metadata (title, start/end times, timezone) and advanced options (recording, breakout sessions, invitees, registration, etc.).
Documentation: https://developer.webex.com/docs/api/v1/meetings/create-a-meeting
Quick Start:
- Obtain an OAuth2 Bearer token with the required scopes (e.g., meeting:schedules_write).
- Send a POST to /v1/meetings with a JSON body including at minimum the meeting start and end times (for scheduled meetings) and title.
Parameters Explained:
- Body fields (common):
  - title (string, required for scheduled meetings): Meeting title/topic.
  - start (string, RFC3339 timestamp) and end (string, RFC3339): Meeting start and end times.
  - timezone (string): IANA timezone (e.g., "America/Los_Angeles").
  - sendEmail (boolean): Whether Webex sends invitation emails (default true).
  - hostEmail (string): If admin-level scopes, create meeting for specified host email.
  - invitees (array): List of invitee objects {"email": "...", "displayName": "..."}.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request: Missing required body fields or invalid timestamp format. Use RFC3339 for times.
- 401 Unauthorized: Missing/invalid/expired token.
- 403 Forbidden: Missing required scope or disallowed operation.
Edge Cases:
- Creating ad-hoc meetings may require adhoc: true + roomId; ad-hoc meetings created with adhoc:true and a roomId have limitations (some cannot be deleted through the Delete endpoint).
- Certain advanced fields (trackingCodes, simultaneousInterpretation, breakoutSessions) may require site/org-level settings and licenses.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Respect Webex API rate limits and quota. For large volumes schedule/queue requests to avoid throttling.
data.evaluateGuide:
Creates a Cisco Webex meeting with its title, timing, timezone, and supported meeting options. Agents can schedule a meeting or create an ad-hoc meeting when supported.
Use for: create a Webex meeting, schedule a meeting, configure meeting options
Not supported: listing meetings, adding a single invitee, deleting meetings

data.name: Create a Meeting Invitee (single)
data.description:
Invite a person to attend a meeting by creating a single meeting invitee.
Documentation: https://developer.webex.com/docs/api/v1/meeting-invitees/create-a-meeting-invitee
Quick Start:
- Obtain an OAuth 2.0 token with meeting:schedules_write (or meeting:admin_schedule_write for admin-level calls).
- POST a JSON body containing meetingId (target meeting) and email (invitee's email). sendEmail defaults to true.
Parameters Explained (body fields):
- meetingId (required): Unique identifier of the meeting series or scheduled meeting to invite the person to.
- email (required): Invitee email address.
- displayName (optional): Display name for the invitee (max length 128). If not specified and the email maps to an existing Webex account, Webex displayName will be used.
- coHost (optional): true if the invitee should be an alternate host/co-host.
- hostEmail (optional): When set by an admin on-behalf-of, indicates which host the invite is for.
- sendEmail (optional): If true (default), sends invitation emails to the invitee.
- panelist (optional): For webinars, marks invitee as panelist when true.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request: Missing required fields (meetingId, email) or invalid email format.
- 401 Unauthorized: Missing/invalid access token.
- 403 Forbidden: Missing required scopes.
- 404 Not Found: meetingId not found or not supported (e.g., scheduled personal room meeting).
Edge Cases:
- meetingId applies to meeting series and scheduled meetings only; does not apply for ended/in-progress meeting instances.
- If the invitee has an existing Webex account, the account displayName will be shown instead of a provided displayName in some clients.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Creating invitees may trigger notification emails; bulk invites are available for large lists (use bulk endpoint).
data.evaluateGuide:
Adds one person as an invitee to a Cisco Webex meeting by meeting ID and email address, with email notification enabled by default. Agents can invite an attendee to an existing meeting.
Use for: invite an attendee, add an email invitee, notify a meeting participant
Not supported: creating meetings, listing invitees, removing invitees

Lists a Zoom user's upcoming meetings within the endpoint's stated time window, including meetings they scheduled or were invited to join. Agents can inspect near-term meeting details.
